meta.label: Protein and sports nutrition
tradeoffLabels: least lead in Consumer Reports' test
meta.attribution: Covers protein powders and ready-to-drink protein shakes sold in the US, with plain Greek yogurt as the food route that needs no supplement. The roster follows the products Consumer Reports tested, so common brands CR did not test, such as Dymatize ISO100, Isopure, Ghost and MyProtein, are not scored here, and the mass gainers, Ensure, Jocko Mölk and the discontinued Momentous products CR tested are left out. Safety scores come from Consumer Reports' October 2025 laboratory test of 23 protein products and its follow-up test of five more. CR bought two to four lots of each anonymously between November 2024 and January 2025 and measured arsenic, cadmium and lead. The score falls in a straight line from 100 for no lead detected to 0 at 200 percent of CR's level of concern for one serving. That level is 0.5 micrograms of lead a day, the California Proposition 65 maximum allowable dose level. It is stricter than the 8.8 micrograms a day that FDA uses as an interim reference level for women of childbearing age and told CR it considers sufficient to apply to all adults. CR states that no federal limit for lead in protein powder exists and that its findings cannot be read as a Prop 65 compliance finding. Consumer Reports describes itself as an independent, nonprofit member organization. The recall score reads FDA's enforcement reports through the openFDA interface, searched on 29 September 2026 for each brand name in the product description and recalling firm fields. It scores the same format under the brand, so a shake recall does not lower a powder's score. Records run from 2012, and a text search can miss a record filed under another product name, so each brand with no record at all is searched in one query that also includes Orgain as a control, which lets a reader see that the search returned something. A brand with no record scores 85, one with only Class II or III records scores 60, one with a Class I record older than five years scores 45, and one with a Class I record inside five years scores 20. FDA defines Class I as a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death. The certification score records only whether a product is in the NSF Certified for Sport register, which NSF says verifies that products contain none of 290 banned substances, that the label matches the contents, that contaminants are not at unsafe levels and that the factory is audited. A product missing from that register is left unscored, because the registers of Informed Sport and Informed Choice, the other main programmes, could not be read for this decision, so absence from NSF does not show a product is untested. Price is per 25 grams of protein at one listed size on one page and date, mostly Target, and it moves between retailers and weeks. Not medical advice. CR's article and its experts state that most adults can meet their protein needs from food, and a doctor or dietitian can advise on individual needs. Reviewed 2026-09. Suggest changes via Contribute.

products.name: Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey (powder)

economical.note: Target lists Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey Protein Powder, Double Rich Chocolate, 22 servings (23.59 oz), at $39.99, with 24 g of protein per serving, which is about $1.89 per 25 g of protein.

safety.note: Consumer Reports' October 2025 test of Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey (chocolate, one 30.5 g scoop) found lead at 56 percent of CR's level of concern per serving. CR lists it under Better Choices for Daily Consumption, with a limit of 1¾ servings a day.

health.note: FDA's enforcement reports, searched through openFDA on 29 September 2026 for the brand name, hold two Class I records for Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey, both dated 7 September 2022, and both for 11 fl oz ready-to-drink shakes made by Lyons Magnus. No record for the powder was found, so the powder scores 85; the shake has its own row.

certification.note: NSF's Certified for Sport register lists Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey Double Rich Chocolate (4.53 kg package, 24 g protein per 30.4 g scoop) and a Vanilla Ice Cream listing in a 4.62 kg package. NSF says the programme verifies that products hold none of 290 banned substances, that the label matches the contents and that contaminants are not at unsafe levels. The register lists the 10 lb sizes, and the 23.59 oz tub priced on this row is not itself shown on the pages read, searched 29 September 2026.

products.description: The best-known whey powder in the US, listed on NSF's register and under Consumer Reports' daily limit for lead, at a middling price per 25 g of protein.

products.name: Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey Protein Shake (ready to drink)

safety.note: Consumer Reports' October 2025 test of Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard Protein Shake (chocolate, one 325 ml carton) found lead at 150 percent of CR's level of concern per serving. CR lists it under Okay to Eat Occasionally, with a limit of 4⅔ servings a week.

health.note: FDA enforcement reports F-1661-2022 and F-1662-2022, dated 7 September 2022, classify the recall of Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard 100% Whey vanilla and chocolate 11 fl oz shakes, made for Optimum Nutrition by Lyons Magnus, as Class I, for findings and potential for Cronobacter sakazakii and Clostridium botulinum. FDA defines Class I as a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death. Both records show a status of Terminated.

products.description: The ready-to-drink shake from the same brand as the powder, which carries a 2022 Class I recall record and a higher lead result than the powder in Consumer Reports' test. No price was read for it.

products.name: BSN Syntha-6 (powder)

safety.note: Consumer Reports' October 2025 test of BSN Syntha-6 Protein Powder (vanilla ice cream, one 47 g scoop) found lead at 46 percent of CR's level of concern per serving, under Better Choices for Daily Consumption, with a limit of 2 servings a day. BSN did not respond to CR's request for comment.

health.note: An openFDA search of FDA's food enforcement reports on 29 September 2026 for Syntha and BSN found no record. One openFDA query for these brand names (Syntha, BSN, Clean Simple Eats, Truvani, Ritual, PlantFusion, Huel, OWYN, Only What You Need, Equip Foods, Thorne, Transparent Labs, KOS) plus Orgain as a control returned four records, all tied to Orgain, so it returned nothing under this brand name.

health.note: FDA enforcement reports dated 18 May 2016 classify as Class I the recall of four Garden of Life Raw Meal organic shake and meal-replacement powders for possible Salmonella contamination, covering 422,923 bottles and units. certification.note: NSF's Certified for Sport register lists Garden of Life Organic Plant-Based Performance Protein in vanilla, chocolate and strawberry. Searched 29 September 2026.
